text:
nina: Quick sync: noticed oscillations again when preemptible nodes join during spikes. Autoscaler treats them as full headroom immediately and allocator repacks, causing churn.
derek: Yep. Similar to previous threads but wanted to propose a lighter-weight stabilization primitive instead of a full admission refactor.
oli: Curious
bout the primitive.
derek: Two-part idea: (1) transient headroom weighting for ephemeral capacity that ramps up over a window; (2) a placement "homogeneity" penalty so the allocator avoids mixing SKU types unless necessary. Keeps changes scoped.
rachael: Sounds reasonable. How would we express the ramp?
derek: Config example:
```yaml
preemptible_stabilization:
  ramp_window: 90s
  start_weight: 0.25
  end_weight: 1.0
  ramp_curve: linear # or exp
  eviction_backoff_after_failure: 120s
```
nina: eviction_backoff_after_failure = per-tenant flag set when a tenant evicted from preemptible within last Xs. That avoids immediate reassign to the same tenant and thrash.
oli: I like backoff. Also propose a placement_hint from allocator: a small struct with "sku_match", "zone_stability", and "frag_score". Admission computes effective_headroom = sum(node_capacity * weight * placement_hint.score).
rachael: keep placement_hint lightweight (0-100 score). Avoid plumbed heavy proto changes. Even a single float in allocator metadata OK.
derek: Agreed. And mix penalty: if a proposed allocation for a tenant would use >1 SKU family, add a penalty factor (0..1) that reduces effective headroom for that allocation path so autoscaler prefers homogeneous fills.
nina: Operationally we need telemetry: preemptible_ramp_time_ms, tenant_eviction_backoff_hits, placement_hint_score_dist, mix_penalty_trigger_count. Those let SRE see if penalization causes capacity waste.
oli: Rollout plan: feature-flagged chain. Step 1: allocator emits placement_hint (score float). Step 2: admission implements ramp weighting using placement_hint. Step 3: small client-visible control: per-tenant flag prefer_no_preemptible. Step 4: mix-penalty in autoscaler/placement heuristics.
derek: Edge cases: very short bursts (<ramp_window) where preemptible is still beneficial for throughput. We can expose a tenant opt-in that says "allow_short_burst_use" so cost-sensitive tenants can still accept preemptible even if ramped low.
nina: Good. Also need to alert when >40% of candidate headroom is preemptible (configurable) so we can catch risky setups.
rachael: Security note: control-plane changes to tenant flags must be audited. Add an audit_event whenever prefer_no_preemptible toggled and when eviction_backoff set/cleared.
oli: Implementation tasks: allocator PR to add placement_hint (small change), admission PR to apply ramp math and backoff check, autoscaler PR to add mix_penalty hook, control-plane PR for tenant QoS flag + audit, dashboards for telemetry (I'll own dashboards).
derek: Simulation: let's run a 10k-tenant sim with varying burst profiles to pick sensible defaults for ramp_window and start_weight. I can wire up a quick sim this week.
nina: I'll draft an RFC capturing config fields, placement_hint schema, telemetry, rollout gating, and the canary plan. Target: RFC by EOW.
rachael: Can we include a short example YAML for per-tenant override?
derek: Sure: 
```yaml
tenant_policies:
  tenant_id: acme-inc
  prefer_no_preemptible: true # defaults to false
  allow_short_burst_use: false
```
ci-bot: Note: created tracking issue <https://go/redwood/tickets/PRJ-4521> and flagged for sprint planning.
nina: thanks. once RFC is up ping here and we'll coordinate PR reviews. Keep the initial default conservative (start_weight 0.25, ramp 90s).
derek: I'll include incremental safety checks: if eviction_rate increases after rollout, auto-disable mix_penalty for that rollout cohort.
rachael: sounds good. end-to-end timeline: RFC (EOW) -> allocator PR (1w) -> admission/autoscaler PRs (2w) -> canary (1w) -> widen (2w) assuming metrics stable.
nina: pinging @oli for dashboard ownership and @rachael for control-plane changes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
